text.en: identify areas where one trade hands work to another.
What layer is being installed now? What layer comes next? What becomes hidden?
sheathing installed → air barrier installed → exterior insulation installed
Once insulation covers the air barrier, a large portion of the membrane becomes difficult to inspect.
Multiple details may apply to the same physical area.
Your QC task is to ensure those documents are coordinated, not read independently.
air barrier + primer + flashing membrane + sealant + insulation adhesive
because incompatible materials can undermine an otherwise correct detail.
overall elevation → specific bay/opening → close-up of detail
because envelope issues are highly location-dependent.
Exterior insulation has already started covering an area where air barrier seams have not been inspected.
Identify area → stop local concealment → expose as required → inspect membrane → document deficiencies → repair → reinspect → photograph → release insulation installation.
The objective is not to create conflict with the trade.
It is to prevent lost inspection opportunity.

qualityObjective.en:
This is the umbrella workflow that coordinates all envelope layers.
Ensure the complete exterior wall assembly is built in the correct sequence, with compatible approved materials, continuous control layers, correct drainage and ventilation paths, and proper integration at openings and interfaces.
A typical exterior wall may include:
interior finish → vapour control → framing → insulation → sheathing → air barrier → exterior insulation → drainage cavity → flashing → cladding/masonry
But the actual Hochelaga assembly must come from the approved project documents.

authorityNote.en: The project drawings, devis, Plan Qualite, PIE/PRIE, approved procedures, professional instructions and CRT/Hydro-Quebec requirements govern. This playbook tells you how to systematically find, verify, document and close the quality requirements; it does not replace them.

text.en: Are there penetrations not yet coordinated?
Will another trade penetrate the membrane tomorrow?
Verify correct product installed in correct location.
Inspect membrane as a continuous plane.
Can air bypass this membrane anywhere?
membrane turned into opening as required;
Membrane around conduit penetration is cut irregularly and not sealed.
Identify → photograph → stop concealment → verify approved penetration detail → install compatible patch/liquid flashing/sealant as specified → reinspect → photograph → release.

qualityObjective.en:
This is one of the highest-priority envelope QC modules.
Create a continuous, durable, properly bonded and sealed air-control layer across the entire envelope, including joints, penetrations, openings and transitions.
The biggest air-barrier failures are rarely in the middle of a large flat membrane.
They occur at:
edges → corners → penetrations → openings → transitions → structural interfaces.

Document → confirm approved repair → patch/seal → reinspect before drywall closes wall → photo → close.
Trend recurring damage by MEP trades or poor coordination.

qualityObjective.en:
Maintain the intended vapour-control layer continuously and in the correct location within the wall/roof assembly to limit moisture migration and condensation risk.
The correct location and permeability depend on the designed wall assembly.
Do not assume “vapour barrier always goes on the warm side” without checking project design.

qualityObjective.en: Install the correct insulation continuously at the required thickness without gaps, compression, moisture damage or thermal bridges beyond what is permitted by the design.

This is exactly where pre-concealment QC saves expensive demolition later.

identify leakage location → document test → determine likely pathway → inspect interfaces → obtain approved corrective method → repair specific defect → retest → document pass → close.

text.en: This one should probably become a dedicated screen in the app.
Every time you inspect the envelope, check these interface zones

Wall ↔ FoundationWall ↔ RoofWall ↔ WindowWall ↔ DoorWall ↔ Structural SteelWall ↔ ConcreteWall ↔ Mechanical penetrationWall ↔ Electrical penetrationMasonry ↔ FlashingCladding ↔ OpeningInsulation ↔ StructureAir barrier ↔ Opening membraneSealant ↔ adjacent materials
Because a large number of envelope failures happen between systems, not within the middle of one system.
Suppose tomorrow the contractor is installing 12 windows.
Your playbook tells you to inspect not just the window.
Sealant pulls away from masonry during adhesion test.
Identify area → review substrate prep/primer/product compatibility → remove failed sealant → prepare joint properly → reprime if required → reinstall → retest adhesion → document.

Sealants look simple but are frequently a major source of envelope failure.
Create durable, properly dimensioned, compatible, well-adhered flexible joints that accommodate movement while maintaining air/water continuity.
